clock.red_title: Red light: keeps your eyes adapted to the dark (observatory, bedroom, server room at night)
clock.full_title: Full screen on or off (key F)
clock.tone_line: For setting clocks without radio or network: a beep on every full second, a long tone on the minute.
clock.tone_running: Running · expected accuracy {acc} (goal ± 5 ms), speaker delay not included.
clock.tone_unsynced: Running · not yet matched with the server – the beeps follow this device's clock for now.
clock.tone_blocked: The browser is still holding the sound – tap “Second beeps” or “Set a clock” once more.
clock.tone_unsupported: Your browser cannot play sound here.
clock.tone_info: The sound only starts after your click (browsers play nothing otherwise). “Second beeps”: a short beep on every full second of server time, a long tone on the full minute. “Set a clock”: a countdown of the last 10 seconds before the full minute, the long tone is 0 – that is when you press the button on the oven, in the car or on your watch. Beeps are scheduled with the browser's audio clock and the measured offset to the server; the expected accuracy is the match (± half the round trip) plus the audio clock's step, goal ± 5 ms. Not included is the delay inside the speaker: Bluetooth headphones and speakers lag 100 to 300 ms, built-in speakers hardly at all.
clock.device_line_unknown: Almost done: the page compares this device's clock with the time server.
clock.device_line_good: Fine – less than 0.1 s off, measured to within {acc}.
clock.device_line_warn: Noticeably off, fine for everyday use: phones usually take the time from the mobile network, PCs from the internet.
clock.device_line_crit: Clearly off: turn on “Set time automatically” in your device settings.
clock.device_info: Like NTP, the page uses four timestamps to measure how far this device's clock is off the server clock (± half the round trip). The result stays in this browser: it is neither stored nor sent to the server or anywhere else. Traffic light: green below 0.1 s, yellow below 1 s, red from 1 s. Phones usually set their clock from the mobile network or NTP, computers from a time server on the internet – depending on the device and the last sync they are milliseconds to seconds off. Some browsers round their clock on purpose (fingerprinting protection, e.g. to 1 ms or 100 ms); small values are less precise then.
clock.egg_possible: 23:59:60 would be possible today: on 30 June and 31 December the last minute (UTC) may get a leap second – none is announced this time.
clock.egg_insert: There is a leap second tonight: 23:59:59 UTC is followed by 23:59:60.
clock.egg_delete: One second is dropped today: 23:59:58 UTC is followed directly by the new day (negative leap second).
clock.stale_detail: the clock keeps running with the last match
clock.band_title: Server: accuracy of the server clock according to chrony. Display: match of this page with the server (± half the round trip of the best of five measurements).
clock.wake_https: Screen lock: can only be disabled over HTTPS
